exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Network Sniffing
exploitedBy.relevance: Unencrypted registry transport allows attackers to capture credentials and layer data via network sniffing.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Web Protocols
exploitedBy.relevance: Downgraded or plaintext HTTP registry communication exposes data to interception over web protocols.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Digital Certificates
exploitedBy.relevance: Absence of mutual TLS means certificate validation is incomplete, enabling attackers to exploit certificate weaknesses during registry push.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Steal or Forge Authentication Certificates
exploitedBy.relevance: Without mutual TLS, forged or stolen certificates can be used to impersonate clients or servers during registry push operations.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: SIP and Trust Provider Hijacking
exploitedBy.relevance: Failure to verify manifest integrity in transit allows attackers to tamper with trust validation mechanisms similar to SIP/trust provider hijacking.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: DLL Search Order Hijacking
exploitedBy.relevance: Unverified layer manifests in transit can allow substitution of malicious content analogous to hijacking legitimate loading processes.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Code Signing
exploitedBy.relevance: Stripping or suppressing cryptographic signatures subverts code signing verification, allowing unsigned or malicious images to be accepted.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Patch System Image
exploitedBy.relevance: Replaying a manipulated manifest or layer push can result in a patched or substituted image being accepted by the registry.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: DNS Server
exploitedBy.relevance: DNS hijacking directly redirects registry traffic to a rogue registry by compromising DNS resolution infrastructure.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Data from Information Repositories
exploitedBy.relevance: Without rate limiting, attackers can enumerate registry contents and harvest layer/manifest data from the repository.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Credentials in Registry
exploitedBy.relevance: Unrestricted enumeration requests can expose stored credentials or sensitive configuration within registry metadata.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Steal Application Access Token
exploitedBy.relevance: Weak or reused credentials transmitted over the network can be intercepted and reused as application access tokens for unauthorized registry pushes.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Application Access Token
exploitedBy.relevance: Compromised registry credentials enable attackers to use application access tokens to authenticate and push malicious images.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Install Root Certificate
exploitedBy.relevance: Without certificate pinning, a rogue CA can install a trusted root certificate to intercept TLS traffic to the registry undetected.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Upload Malware
exploitedBy.relevance: Chunked upload resumption without integrity checks allows an attacker to inject malicious content into a partially uploaded layer.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Build Image on Host
exploitedBy.relevance: Lack of integrity checkpoints during resumable uploads can enable a malicious image to be assembled and stored in the registry.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Multi-hop Proxy
exploitedBy.relevance: An insecure pull-through cache or proxy in the transit path can act as a multi-hop proxy to intercept and modify registry traffic.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Poisoned Pipeline Execution
exploitedBy.relevance: A compromised pull-through cache can serve poisoned image layers to consumers, effectively poisoning the delivery pipeline.
